title: Minimal replay decision brief for customers — 2029-07-01
content:
Purpose:
This note is a short, customer-facing brief describing choices available after the recent inference divergence incident (KV cache divergence leading to partial replay of prior responses). Goal is to give each affected tenant a compact set of options, the verification steps we provide, and an evidence package they can use to decide whether to accept a rollforward, request a replay, or opt-out.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Event: On 2029-06-23 03:10–04:35 UTC we observed inconsistent outputs for a subset of streaming and bulk inference requests due to a KV cache divergence introduced during a deployment rolling update.
- Impact: ~0.8% of requests across affected regions returned stale token prefixes or duplicated snippets; latency largely within SLOs. No data exfiltration detected.
- Current status: serving routing fixed (2029-06-23 05:10 UTC), KV reconciliation job completed (2029-06-23 08:40 UTC). Customers can pick from three remediation paths below.

What happened (short):
- During a canary promotion we shipped a runtime change that changed how KV lifetimes were tracked for long-lived sessions. An edge-case in the eviction logic allowed older KV prefixes to be served alongside new prefixes for the same session id when requests were replayed through a routing fallback. That created occasional prefix duplication or stale completions.
- Root cause: mismatch between eviction TTL and routing fallback cache promotion logic.

Impact details for customers:
- Affected tenants: those with long-running streaming sessions and bulk replay jobs between 2029-06-23 03:05–04:40 UTC in us-west1 and eu-west2.
- Symptom examples: truncated structured outputs (missing final block), repeated sentence fragments, or duplicated suggested actions.
- Severity: Mostly functional correctness (noise), not security or availability.

Customer choices (decision matrix):
A) Accept rollforward (default) — no action required
- What it is: Continue with the state after reconciliation. Ideal when inconsistencies were cosmetic and volume small.
- Pros: Fast, no reprocessing.
- Cons: If you need exact reproducibility for events in the window, this does not change existing responses.

B) Request controlled replay (recommended if you require canonical outputs)
- What it is: Redwood will re-run affected requests through the reconciled runtime and deliver regenerated responses.
- Pros: Produces canonical results; we include a diff/evidence bundle.
- Cons: Re-run cost (billed at standard inference rates); potential for slightly different non-deterministic outputs depending on model variant (we use same pinned model+seed policy where possible).

C) Opt-out and self-verify (for customers who prefer to keep originals)
- What it is: No changes to your stored responses. We provide an evidence bundle so you can independently validate whether you want to replay.
- Pros: Zero compute re-run cost, immediate stability.
- Cons: You retain the original inconsistent outputs.

Evidence package we provide (what you will receive for any tenant request):
- Time-indexed request log (request id, timestamp, session id) for the window.
- Pairwise diffs for any resubmitted requests (if replayed).
- Hashes of model outputs before and after reconciliation to validate changes.
- Small sample of raw token streams for forensic verification.

How to choose quickly:
- If your app is prompt-append or stateful (session history matters), choose B.
- If outputs were used only for analytics or low-risk surfacing, choose A.
- If you need time to audit, choose C and request the evidence package, then decide within 7 days.

Operational notes and verification steps we recommend customers run: (we provide scripts in the linked gist)
1) Fetch request list for your tenant from the evidence bundle.
2) Identify high-priority requests by traffic or revenue impact.
3) For sample requests, compare pre/post hashes; if hashes differ, examine token diffs and decide if semantic change matters.

Compensation and billing:
- Replay runs performed by Redwood for customers who select option B will be billed at our standard inference rate but we will apply a 40% credit on replay compute for requests originating in the incident window as a gesture of goodwill.

Timeline (concise):
- 2029-06-23 02:58 UTC — rolling update started (canary).
- 2029-06-23 03:10 UTC — first anomaly detected by internal monitoring (token duplication alerts).
- 2029-06-23 03:22 UTC — automatic rollback of canary to previous runtime for all regions.
- 2029-06-23 04:05 UTC — manual verification; found cache promotion mismatch.
- 2029-06-23 05:10 UTC — routing rules tightened; fallback paths disabled.
- 2029-06-23 08:40 UTC — reconciliation job completed.

FAQ (short):
Q: Will replay change customer-visible billing?
A: Replays are billed but with a 40% compute credit for affected window; storage/ingress charges unchanged.
Q: Will data be lost?
A: No — original responses are preserved; replays create additional results that you can choose to adopt.
Q: How long do I have to choose?
A: 7 days from this notice. If we do not hear back we will perform a conservative rollforward (option A).

Next steps (what Redwood will do):
- Send tenant-specific evidence bundles within 24 hours (starts 2029-07-01 09:00 UTC).
- Provide a one-click request form (link in tenant bundle) to opt into a replay.
- Start replay jobs for opted-in tenants within 48 hours of request.

Owner and contact: Aisha Thompson (customer-success lead) — aisha.thompson@redwood.ai — include "Replay Decision" in subject line.

Appendix: quick verification checklist for engineers (we'll include runnable snippets):
- Download evidence bundle -> run hash-checker -> open sample token diffs -> approve replay if semantic mismatch is material.

Notes to internal teams (short):
- Engineering: follow up with a permanent fix to the eviction/promotion contract; target patch release 2029-07-05.
- Product: review communication cadence and default policy for 7-day opt-out windows.
- CS: prioritize outreach to top-20 affected tenants within 6 hours of this doc.

End of brief.
